sentences: The family physician recounts to the detective and the doctor in the detective's lodgings the legend of the Hell hound that killed the devilish ancestor in retaliation for his misdeeds, including murdering the daughter of a servant.

He asks the detective to investigate the death of his friend the late baronet, in the moorland region, from heart failure, in the moor surrounding his estate, the ancestral hall, with a look of horror on his face.

The family physician fears for the life of the young baronet, the late baronet's nephew and heir, who's just come from a distant colony to take possession of his inheritance and of the ancestral hall.
Although sceptical, the detective and the doctor agree to meet the young baronet who complains that one of his boots is missing.
The family physician tells them that the family estate is worth about £1,000,000.
A peculiar threat from a dangerous tarantula convinces the detective that the young baronet's life is in danger.
Claiming that he cannot come to the ancestral hall himself, the detective dispatches the doctor to the moorland region with the family physician and the young baronet.
The detective tells the young baronet not to go out onto the moor after dark.
On their way to the ancestral hall, the trio learns that the convict, a convicted murderer, has escaped the nearby prison and is hiding on the moor.
At the ancestral hall, the manservant, the butler, and the manservant's wife, the housekeeper show them around the mansion.
One of two portraits of the ancestor is missing, and the servant couple say it was mysteriously stolen months before.
The next day, the young baronet and the doctor meet the clergyman, a bishop and keen entomologist.
The doctor gets trapped in a patch of mire in the great bog and is saved by a farmer named the neighbour and his daughter the young woman, a girl who bewitches the young baronet.
That night, the doctor and the young baronet investigate a light on the moor.
They briefly encounter a strange man who flees in the shadows, and a distant hound howls, provoking in the young baronet a mild heart attack.
The doctor spots a man on a hill in the distance while helping the young baronet back to the ancestral hall.
The doctor discovers it to be the detective, who has concealed his own arrival to investigate more freely.
The convict, wearing the young baronet's clothes, is slaughtered by the unseen hound.
The detective and the doctor find his body mutilated in a ritual, and the legendary curved dagger of the ancestor.
The servant couple confess to have helped the convict, who was their relative, by supplying food and clothes each time he signaled with a light from his hideout.
The detective is convinced that neither the servant couple nor the convict are connected to the death of the late baronet.
He also figures that the tarantula found in the city was stolen from the clergyman.
After surviving personal danger in an abandoned tin mine while looking for evidence of a hound, the detective is able to deduce who unleashed the hound in pursuit of the late baronet.
The detective explains about questioning the manservant about the missing portrait; it was stolen because it revealed the fingers on the ancestor's right hand were webbed just like the neighbour's.
Finding the dagger stolen, the detective and the doctor follow the young baronet and the young woman to the moor.

The young woman takes the young baronet to the ruins where the detective and the doctor hear the young woman reveal her intentions to a horrified young baronet, revealing that she and her father are also descendants of the ancestor, planning to claim the inheritance as their own once the young baronet is dead.
The hound appears and attacks the young baronet, until the detective shoots it, causing it to back off.
With the ancestor's curved dagger, the neighbour attempts to attack the doctor, who shoots and wounds him.
The wounded hound attacks the neighbour and fatally mauls him.
The detective shoots and kills the hound.
The young baronet is unscathed from the mauling as the detective reveals the hound to be an ordinary dog wearing a mask to make it look more terrifying.
The young woman tries to flee across the moor, only to fall into the great bog and sink to her death as the detective and the doctor take a shocked young baronet back to the ancestral hall.
Back in the detective's lodgings, the detective and the doctor are given by the young baronet the stolen portrait of the ancestor that was found on the neighbour's farm.
The film begins in a theatre, where a pianist begins to play a piano accompaniment to the actual film being shown in the theater.

The detective has just restored a stolen artifact to three French nuns, and is later called on a case by the family physician concerning the young baronet and a legendary hound that curses the family estate.
Tired and worn out by so many cases, the detective passes the case onto the doctor, who is portrayed as a Welsh eccentric.

On their way from the station to the hall, the young baronet, the family physician, the doctor and the coachman (their driver) are halted by a policeman, who warns them of a murderer stalking the moors, before sending the group on their way.
While out in the moor collecting specimens, the doctor has a curious encounter in a hut with the raving recluse and the recluse's exceedingly strong lover, the mistress.

In the next scene, we see the detective still in the city, visiting the old woman, his mother, who, as a bogus spiritualist aided by her housekeeper, the assistant, scams older ladies of their money in false seances.
The detective's mother is concerned that "the doctor's nickname" (the doctor) may need help, and that "her son's nickname" (as she calls her son), should rush to his aid.
In next scene, the detective interviews the one-legged applicant (also played by the lead actor) to act as a runner on the moor.
In the next scene, while wandering on the moors, the doctor happens upon the neighbour, who mistakes him for the young baronet.

The neighbour's sister describes dramatically her encounter with the Hound on the moor, suggesting that it ravished her, whereupon she attempts to force herself upon the reluctant doctor, with the neighbour's sister undergoing supernatural transformations reminiscent of a well-known horror film.
The servant couple at the ancestral hall mistreat the young baronet and the doctor, feeding them only cheese and water and then throwing them into a small bedroom, ankle-deep in water.
The doctor then goes to the village to send a message to the detective (who is during this time visiting his cranky mother), and meets the neighbour of the nearby manor.
The neighbour is carrying a chihuahua that proceeds to urinate in the doctor's pocket and face.
Arriving at the nearby manor, the doctor meets the eccentric neighbour's wife, who displays surreal symptoms suggesting demonic possession.
Late at night, the young baronet and the doctor discover the neighbours and the escaped murderer, whom the doctor recognizes as the female servant's brother the convict, having a family dinner.
Oddly enough, neither of the men seems to panic at this.
Afterward, the detective arrives and examines the case so far.
An invitation arrives for the young baronet, asking him to dinner at the nearby manor.
Suspecting a trap, the doctor goes along with the young baronet while the detective observes carefully.
The neighbour's wife resumes her bizarre acts and begins to vomit pale-blue liquid over the young baronet, whilst the neighbour's chihuahua urinates in the doctor's soup.
Ordered to leave in disgrace, the neighbours, the family physician, the recluse, and the mistress follow the young baronet and the doctor to kill them, but become trapped in a quagmire.
The detective then proceeds to reveal that the Hound is no more than a large, rather friendly Irish Wolfhound owned by the late baronet, whose excited barking was misinterpreted as a monstrous beast.
He also states that the dog is the sole heir of the late baronet.
With the dog gone, the would-be murderers would have gained the family fortune and the estate.
The film ends on the pianist, who is then hit by vegetables from the audience.
The old lord suffers a heart attack after being terrorised by the notorious hound of the family, a portent of doom for the male heirs of the family castle.
When the family solicitor sends word to his nephew, the heir, that he should attend a reading of the will, the man servant adds a message warning him to stay away.
He has been working with the villain, another family relative, in his plan to kill everyone who stands in the way of him inheriting the castle.
The villain has been keeping the hound in an underground lair, and has also prepared various bombs to use against the heir if he arrives.
The heir saves the young woman when her horses bolt and they start courting.
The heir sends for the detective in a letter, but the villain blows up the postbox and disguises himself as the detective.
The real detective reads in the newspaper about his supposed arrival in the county and decides to check it out.
The villain plants a bomb in a light fitting.
The detective defuses the bomb with a shot from a pistol.
The villain blames the man servant for the attack.
The villain then tries poisoning the heir and the young woman but the detective fires his pistol at the glasses.
The man servant is blamed once again.
Investigating the villain's room the detective discovers a secret diary revealing his plans.
Finding the detective in his room, the villain activates a hidden trapdoor by turning a vase which drops the detective into the lair of the hound.
The detective then kills the hound and escapes.
He then disguises himself as the villain.
The villain confronts the detective and removes his disguise.
The man servant disguised as a suit of armour captures the villain.
The detective shows everyone the diary and the villain is arrested.
The movie revolves around the unwanted incidents that happen in the princely state.
After the murder of the king, the doctor asks for help from the detective, a family friend.
The detective sends his assistant to the princely state to investigate and ascertain the security of the young prince, the new successor of the royal family of the estate.
They observe that a mysterious lady, the singer, sings uncanny song while wandering around the adjacent water body.
The neighbour, a suspicious botanist, who stays in the neighbourhood also roams in that locality.
It is revealed that he was deprived of real property of the royal family and took revenge by killing the members of the family.
He uses a deaf and dumb porter as a hired killer.
Ultimately, he is killed by the detective at the end before he could commit another murder.

Between 1979 and 1986, Soviet television produced a series of five films at the state movie studio, split into eleven episodes, starring the first lead actor as the detective and the second lead actor as the doctor.
The last film, the story of the coming century, was shown in cinemas in 1987 (as the film of the detective in the new century), ahead of its 1988 television premiere.

The series ran as follows: 1979 the film about the detective and the doctor 1st episode: "the episode of the first meeting" (based on "the story of the snake"). 2nd episode: "the episode of the writing in blood" (based on "the first novel"). 1980 the adventure film about the detective and the doctor 1st episode: "the episode of the blackmailer" (based on "the story of the blackmailer"). 2nd episode: "the episode of the fight" (based on "the story of the last case"). 3rd episode: "the episode of the hunt" (based on "the story of the empty house"). 1981 the adventure film about the detective and the doctor: the story of the hound.
Two episodes based on "the story of the hound". 1983 the adventure film about the detective and the doctor: the story of the treasure.
Two episodes based on "the second novel" and "the story of the scandal". 1987 the adventure film about the detective and the doctor: the story of the coming century.
Two episodes based on "the story of the engineer", "the story of the stain", "the story of the stolen plans" and "the story of the farewell".
The script was written by the first screenwriter and the second screenwriter on their own initiative.
The director was not a big fan of the author's work, but he liked the idea of a future TV movie.

In addition, there was an interesting juxtaposition of characters in the script the detective and the doctor, which was supposed to attract the viewer and what, according to the director, previous film adaptations lacked.
The detective is opposed to the official police system of the police headquarters, because the main thing for him is to help, not just to punish.

This, it seems to me, is the secret of the enduring love of readers and viewers for the detective, the living personification of loyalty and reliability — qualities that people have always needed so much.
That was the reason why we were so willing to work on these films.
Unlike some of their Western counterparts, the films are very close to the literary source.

Some of the departures include the detective's easy-going and humorous demeanor, as well as comic relief provided by some of the characters (most notably that of the baronet and his butler in the story of the hound episode).
The first lead actor and the second lead actor met at the auditions, and they immediately formed friendly relations: In relation to life, we coincided in many ways.
The second lead actor shared with me deeply personal experiences, and I think he did not share these experiences with anyone else… Love can be played on the screen.
And friendship is impossible to play.
You need to be friends.
A street in the old city doubles as the detective's street (the same street was used for exterior locations of another fictional street in "the spy series").
Many scenes were filmed in the large northern city and the nearby capital city.
"The role" of the famous waterfall was "performed" by a mountain waterfall in the southern region.
In the 19th century, the doctor has been medically discharged from the Army and moves to the city.
The doctor is introduced to the detective by a fellow student of the hospital, and becomes interested in his investigative principles.
The detective invites the doctor to share his new flat in a central street, which the doctor accepts.

In 1895, the inspector arrives and presents the detective and the doctor with a puzzling case: the dead woman, a consumptive woman in bridal dress, had fired on by-passers in the street from a balcony before fatally shooting herself.
Later that evening, her husband was confronted by the dead woman, who shot him dead before disappearing into the fog.
Fascinated by the dead woman's apparent survival, the detective takes the case.
At the morgue, the pathologist informs the detective that the woman who killed herself, the woman who murdered her husband and the body on hand have all been positively identified as the dead woman.
When the Bride apparently returns to murder other men, the detective deduces that these are copycat crimes.
Months later, the detective's brother refers a case to him: the lady's husband, the nobleman, appeared terrified when he received an envelope full of orange pips (seeds).
When she asked what it means, he initially said "death" but then brushed it off as "nothing."
Two subsequent episodes occurred at night.
In the first the nobleman was again terrified and claimed to have seen the Bride outside the windows.
In the second, the lady found him out on the grounds, transfixed by the Bride standing before him, her face covered by a veil.
The Bride – who he identified as the dead woman – threatened him with death, but when he fell to the ground in a faint, she disappeared.
When the detective and the doctor meet with him, the nobleman is uncooperative, claiming that he sleepwalks and describing his wife as "an hysteric."
The detective and the doctor stake out the house for the evening.
When a ghostly-looking Bride appears and disappears in front of them, they hear the sound of breaking glass, followed by screams from both the nobleman and the lady.
They discover the nobleman stabbed to death by what appears to be the dead woman, who then escapes through a broken window.
The inspector arrives and observes a note attached to the dagger, which the detective says was not there when he found the body.
The note reads, "Miss me?", a phrase used by the modern-day arch-criminal.
After insisting that the case's solution is so simple that even the inspector could solve it, the detective meditates.
The arch-criminal appears and insults the detective about the mystery of the dead woman's apparent post-suicide revival, alluding to his similar apparent death in the present.
The arch-criminal appears to shoot himself in the head but remains alive.
In the present day, it is revealed that the events of the Victorian country are actually occurring within the detective's drug-laden Mind Palace.

The plane has returned to the country minutes after taking off after the arch-criminal's broadcast, and the detective's brother, the doctor, and the doctor's wife enter the plane to find a frustrated detective rambling about the unsolved dead woman's case.
The detective explains he had hoped to solve the case, believing it would prove crucial to solving the arch-criminal's return.
The Victorian detective awakens, with an awareness of events of the present as a seeming hallucination induced by cocaine.
He receives a telegram from the doctor's wife saying she has found the dead woman's co-conspirators at a desanctified church.
There, the detective and the doctor discover and interrupt a secret group of the Women's Rights Movement, whose members include the pathologist, a female acquaintance, and the doctor's maidservant.
The detective explains that they used a double to fake the dead woman's death, allowing her to kill her husband and create the persona of the avenging ghost Bride.
Already dying, she was later killed at her request by being shot through the mouth.
The duplicate corpse was replaced by the dead woman's actual corpse, the one the detective and the doctor saw at the morgue, for a positive identification.
Since then, the women have used the persona of the Bride to murder men who wronged them.
The detective surmises that the lady, being a member of the society, killed her husband.
He makes his accusation to the approaching Bride, assuming that it is the lady.
When he lifts the bride's veil, however, he finds that the "Bride" is actually the arch-criminal, who tells him the scenario doesn't make sense because "it's not real".
The detective reawakens in the present, where he insists on finding the dead woman's grave to prove that her body-double was buried under the coffin.
While digging, he hears the dead woman's corpse repeatedly whisper "Do not forget me".
The corpse moves to attack him, leading the detective to realize he is not actually awake.
He then "awakens" in the past on a ledge next to the waterfall.
At the antiquities museum, the Chinese pottery expert sees something frightening and disappears.
Meanwhile, the detective takes the doctor to a high-powered international finance house.
There, the financier, an old university acquaintance of the detective's, asks for help.
A break-in occurred in which a seemingly meaningless pair of symbols were spray-painted onto a portrait of a banker.
The detective realises it was a message meant for one man – the trader of the overseas desk – who has not come to work.
The detective breaks into the trader's locked flat and finds him dead.
The police, under the detective inspector, regard it as a suicide, though the detective sees it as murder.
Soon, the journalist (an actor) is killed inside his locked flat.
The detective and the doctor investigate, and in a library where the journalist had been, they find the same mysterious symbols painted on a shelf.
The doctor, seeking financial security, obtains a job as locum at a local surgery run by the physician.
Later, the detective and the doctor discover a link between the two men; both had just returned from the eastern country, and both went to an oriental curio shop, "the cat shop".
There, the detective learns that the symbols are ancient Chinese city numerals (correctly another city's numerals).
The detective notices that the pottery expert's flat is empty and snoops around, where he finds an intruder; a brief fight ensues, but the attacker flees.
At the museum, they then discover the same symbols on a statue.
Then, with the help of the graffiti artist, the detective and the doctor find more symbols graffitied on a wall and struggle to decode the message.
Back at the museum, the detective surprises the pottery expert in hiding, who explains the code is linked to the criminal ring "the smuggling gang", of which she was once a member.
Unfortunately, before she can fully decode the message, she is killed by her brother, another criminal gang member.
The detective realises the trader and the journalist were members of the smuggling gang, involved in smuggling valuable antiquities to sell in the city.
They were killed because one of them stole something.
The detective knows the message is in the form of a book cipher, and he and the doctor spend the night going through the first two victims' books, trying to find the solution.
The doctor's first day at work does not go well, but the physician covers for him, and they organise to go out on a date.
The detective arranges tickets to a travelling Chinese circus.

While the doctor and the physician enjoy the classic escapology and acrobatics acts, the detective snoops around backstage and is attacked, but with the physician and the doctor's help, the three escape.

While the detective continues to search for the solution to the book cipher, the doctor and the physician are kidnapped; the doctor is mistaken for the detective by the villains, who want him to reveal the location of the missing "treasure" in return for the physician's life.
Fortunately, the detective cracks the code using a city street guide, and rescues the doctor and the physician.

He also realises the elusive "treasure" has been in plain sight all the time: A jade hairpin belonging to the Chinese royal family, worn by the trader's secretary/mistress, who had received it as a gift from the trader.
However, the ringleader, the smuggling gang's leader, escapes and contacts a person via online "chat" identified only by an initial who had helped the gang to get a foothold in the city.
The ringleader states that even though they were compromised by the detective she will not reveal his identity.
The unnamed person responds with "I am certain" as a sniper's red dot settles on her forehead.
As the screen goes black a shot is heard.

Two years after his supposed death (depicted in "an earlier episode"), the detective has been completely absolved of the slanderous accusations against him originated by the arch-criminal and secretly returns to the city to help his brother uncover an apparently imminent terrorist attack.

An interleaved scene shows a version of how the detective might have faked his death: by jumping from the roof with a bungee cable, bouncing back and entering the building through a window, leaving the arch-criminal's body with a detective mask to mislead the doctor and other onlookers, the doctor himself being hypnotised by a famous hypnotist to give the time for this to be set up.
This version of events is quickly shown to be a conspiracy theory invented by the forensic officer, who feels responsible for the detective's death.
The doctor now has a girlfriend, to whom he intends to propose in a restaurant.
At this point, the detective, disguised as a French waiter, approaches the couple but is not immediately recognised by the doctor.
When the detective reveals his identity, the doctor attacks him three times in three different locations.

When the doctor refuses to accept his explanations, the detective enlists the pathologist to assist him in his next case, that of an underground skeleton behind a desk containing a manuscript: a confession by a notorious killer, revealed toward the end of the episode to be a fake planted by the forensic officer to lure the detective out of hiding.

Later that day, the girlfriend receives a text in a skip code (first and every three words) telling her that the doctor has been kidnapped by unknown assailants and will die if he is not rescued in time, along with a coded location.
The detective and the girlfriend come to his rescue on a motorcycle and manage to drag him out of a lit bonfire on which a "guy" (effigy of a historical plotter) was about to be burned.

The detective is shown a video by an underground railway employee of the mysterious vanishing of a passenger from a train between two stations near the parliament and later identifies the passenger as a member of the upper house, the peer, whom he knows to be a foreign agent and who has been acting unusually.

He notices that it is not only the peer who vanished but an entire carriage of the train and deduces that the attack will be on the parliament building, which will be holding a late-night hearing on a new anti-terrorism bill on Guy Fawkes Night, 5 November.
The detective and the doctor enter the abandoned station near the parliament, finding the secretly diverted carriage.
It is rigged with explosives to make an enormous bomb.

The detective manages to defuse the bomb by turning the off-switch, but not before making the doctor believe the bomb can't be defused, leading the detective to apologize to the doctor for getting him involved and saying that the doctor would have had a future if he hadn't come back.
This all had the intended effect of causing the doctor to panic and reveal to the detective how much he has missed him, to the doctor's later embarrassment.
Another scene intercut with the above shows the detective visiting the forensic officer.
He reveals how he faked his death as part of a scheme to convince the arch-criminal of his lost credibility and demise.
The plan allowed the two brothers to dissolve the arch-criminal's network successfully.

The detective tells the forensic officer that he and his brother had anticipated thirteen possible scenarios that could happen on the roof, and that while the doctor's view was obstructed, members of his network of homeless helpers rolled out an inflatable mattress and took their roles as shocked bystanders and paramedics.
With the aid of a squash ball under his arm to temporarily stop his pulse, the detective convincingly faked his death.
The forensic officer casts doubt on the integrity of this version of events, arguing it would be nearly impossible to ensure the doctor remained exactly where the detective wanted.
The forensic officer points out that he is "the last person" the detective would tell, but as he turns around, the room is empty.
The forensic officer then begins tearing his theories from the wall, laughing hysterically, and the intercut scene ends.
The peer is ambushed by the police and arrested after leaving his hotel suite.
The doctor asks the detective who abducted him and why, questions for which the detective has no answers yet.
In the final scene, a bespectacled man with blue eyes is seen observing footage of the detective and the girlfriend rescuing the doctor from the fire.
A young girl wakes up on an aeroplane and finds everybody asleep.
Panic stricken, she answers a ringing mobile phone, only to hear the voice of the arch-criminal announce, "Welcome to the final problem".

After the detective stages a break-in at the elder brother's home and tricks the elder brother into revealing the sister's existence, the elder brother reveals that, like himself and the detective, the sister was also born with advanced intellectual abilities, even describing her as an era-defining genius on a par with a famous scientist.
However, she also has a total lack of normal sensation and emotion.
After she kidnapped and killed the detective's dog, the childhood pet, and set their house on fire, the detective's parents sent the sister to a mental institution.

But the elder brother reveals that, behind their parents' backs, he had the sister transferred to the island prison, a government "black site" and maximum-security "prison within a prison" in the northern sea.
The whole experience had been so deeply traumatising to the detective that his memories of her had been “rewritten”.
Their conversation is interrupted when a quadcopter carrying a motion-activated grenade flies into the detective's flat.
The doctor, the detective, and the elder brother flee as the bomb detonates, blasting the detective and the doctor out of the windows.

Later, the doctor and the detective hijack a fishing trawler to travel to the island prison, carrying out a diversionary plan so that the detective can reach the sister's cell with the elder brother disguising himself as a fisherman.
The elder brother and the doctor corner the prison governor, discovering that he has explicitly disobeyed the elder brother's protocol and has allowed the sister to interact with prison staff.
Using her skill to "reprogram" everyone she speaks with, the sister has effectively ruled the prison.
Meanwhile, the detective talks to the sister; but after toying with him, particularly about the childhood pet's death, she attacks him and knocks him unconscious.
The guards lock the detective, the doctor, the elder brother, and the governor together in the sister's old cell.

It is then revealed that five years prior, the elder brother granted the sister an unsupervised five-minute interview with the arch-criminal as a Christmas present, in exchange for her detecting national security threats to the country.
During that time, the arch-criminal agreed to record video messages for her.
The doctor wakes up in the sister’s cell with the detective, the elder brother, and the governor, and the young girl's distress call comes through the speakers.
The detective tries to talk to the girl, but the sister stops the call.

After forcing the governor to kill himself, the sister mentally torments the detective, the elder brother, and the doctor, forcing them into cruel and deadly games to save their lives while videos of the arch-criminal taunt them.

Although the sister forces the detective to continue with the prospect of saving the girl on the aeroplane, he eventually stops the games by threatening to shoot himself when she orders him to murder either the doctor or the elder brother.
Furious, the sister has the three of them shot with tranquilliser darts.
The detective wakes up near the burnt-out wreckage of his family's old house.
He speaks to the girl in the aeroplane to guide her in landing safely.
The doctor wakes up chained at the bottom of a well.
As the sister raises the water level in the well, the doctor finds a child's skull there.
The detective realizes that what he thought was his dog the childhood pet was his childhood friend, the boy.
The childhood pet was the boy's name when they played as pirates, and the sister threw him into the well and left him for dead because she felt left out of the detective's game.

The detective then figures out where the sister is hiding by deciphering the real meaning of the song that the sister had taunted him with when the boy went missing, which reveals that she wants him to find her.
It is also revealed that the little girl on the aeroplane has been the sister all along, and the game was a cry for help, for whenever she closes her eyes she's on the plane and all alone.
After helping her and rescuing the doctor, the detective sends her back to the island prison.
The elder brother explains to his and the detective's parents, who are furious that he told them the sister was dead, that she refuses to speak to people anymore.
The detective visits the sister, and they play the violin together instead of talking.
While helping the detective repair his destroyed flat, the doctor finds another video sent by the doctor's wife before she died.

The detective and the doctor watch as the doctor's wife explains posthumously that, whatever kind of person they may be, they will always be her boys of the famous street – "the detective and the doctor", the series ending with the flat restored and the two resuming to their lives of solving mysteries.
The detective is bored without stimulating cases.
The detective's brother urges the detective to investigate the death of the intelligence service clerk and the disappearance of a flash drive containing missile plans.
The detective refuses and then is called to police headquarters where the inspector hands him an envelope containing a mobile phone identical to the victim's phone from "an earlier case".
The phone shows a photo of a derelict room, which the detective recognises as the unoccupied flat 221c, downstairs from 221b.
The detective, the doctor and the inspector enter the room and find a pair of trainers in the middle of the floor.
The mobile rings, and the caller – a frightened hostage reading texts from her captor – states that if the detective cannot solve the puzzle in twelve hours, a bomb will kill her.
After closely examining the shoes, the detective realises they belonged to the dead boy, a schoolboy who drowned in a swimming pool 20 years previously.
Evidence on the laces indicates that botulinum toxin was introduced into the boy's eczema medication, leading to his paralysis.
The detective announces the solution to the bomber, and the hostage is freed.
A second message shows a blood-stained sports car, and another hostage phones, giving the detective eight hours to solve this mystery.
Finding the vehicle without its driver, the detective interviews the missing man's wife and the manager of the agency where the car had been rented.
After finding that the blood in the car had been frozen, the detective announces that the missing man paid the rental agency owner to help him disappear, and the hostage is freed.
A third message and hostage point the detective to the recent death of the TV presenter, who allegedly died from tetanus.
The doctor interviews the presenter's brother, and the detective shows that the housekeeper — the presenter's brother's lover — murdered the presenter by increasing the dosage of her botox injection.
Despite the detective solving the puzzle, the hostage is killed, along with several others, for describing the kidnapper's voice.
The fourth message is a photograph of the river, but no hostage calls.
The detective and the police discover the security guard's body on the riverbank.
The detective claims that the security guard was strangled by an assassin called the "strangler".
He also deduces that the security guard worked at a local art gallery that is preparing to display an allegedly "lost" old master's painting.

The doctor visits the security guard's flat and finds he was interested in astronomy but not art and that a recent message on his answering machine from a professor stated that he'd been right about something.
The detective deduces that the old master's painting is a forgery and that the security guard's discovery of it was why he was killed.
The hostage calls and the detective gives his answer, but the hostage, a child, begins counting down.
Realizing he must prove his deduction, the detective spots a supernova in the painting that actually appeared 200 years after the old master, thus saving the child.
The museum curator confesses setting up the forgery and outs her accomplice: a man named "the mastermind".

At the detective's brother's insistence, the doctor investigates the clerk's death, and he and the detective track down the thief, the brother of the clerk's fiancée, who admits to stealing the flash drive and accidentally killing the clerk when he was confonted.
Unable to sell it, the thief kept the drive and gives it to the detective.
Realizing that the clerk's death and the missing flash drive were the fifth mystery, the detective texts the bomber, offering to turn over the device.
But at the meeting place, it is the doctor who arrives as the fifth hostage, wearing an explosive vest.
The mastermind – who'd been seen earlier as the pathologist's new boyfriend – appears and introduces himself as "a specialist, just like you."
After taunting and threatening the detective, the mastermind leaves but returns after the detective removes the doctor's vest.
